newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian M2 money supply up 4.97 pct in April.
newsitem.headline: Romanian M2 money supply up 4.97 pct in April.

text.p: Romania's M2 money supply rose by 4.97 percent in April after staying almost unchanged in March as cash in circulation saw a seasonal upswing, central bank (BNR) data showed on Wednesday.
M2 -- Romania's measure of broad money supply -- was 39.75 trillion lei at end-April, or up 100.77 percent year-on-year and 31 percent from end-1996, BNR data showed.
The broad money's rise was lower than monthly inflation which slowed to 6.9 percent in April after hitting a record 30.7 percent in March following price liberalisation.
Cash in circulation soared by 14.2 percent to 5.4 trillion lei in April following wage indexation for the second quarter this year and bonuses ahead of Orthodox Easter.
The surge in cash in circulation led a 12.83 percent rise to 10.1 trillion lei of the M1 narrow money, which includes curreny outside banks and demand deposits.
Demand deposits went up by 11.3 percent to 4.68 trillion lei in April, reversing a 7.3 percent fall the previous month.

Household savings saw a 9.75 percent rise to 12.1 trillion lei in April, close to a 9.6 percent increase in March, with banks' deposit rates still attractive despite a downtrend to about 115 percent from about 135 percent earlier this year.

Residents' hard currency deposits were almost flat at 13.9 trillion lei in April. Their stake in April's broad money fell to 35 percent in April from 36.5 percent in March, with the domestic leu currency stabilising near 7,050 to the dollar.
ROMANIAN MONEY SUPPLY APRIL 97 MARCH 97 APRIL 96
NOTE: M2 is Romania's measure of broad money. Inflation was 6.9 percent in April, down from a record 30.7 percent in March when prices for fuel, staples and energy were liberalised.
